rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a 3BA blastocyst and correctly notes expansion and a looser ICM, but it overstates visibility/precision of the ICM location and TE uniformity from this single image and adds details not clearly discernible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior miscarriage, male factor context, BMI, lifestyle, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall structure is logical, but several probability adjustments are speculative and the final estimate may be overly pessimistic for a 26-year-old with a good Day-5 blastocyst; some claims are stronger than the evidence supports.

Mostly aligned on morphology, lifestyle counseling, and general transfer planning, but includes debatable/non-routine recommendations such as broad thrombophilia testing after one miscarriage, ERA, routine PGT-A at age 26, and intralipid/NK-cell-based interventions.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer assessment, lifestyle modification, and contingency planning, though some suggested investigations/interventions are more aggressive than standard practice.
